item.title: How a Walmart Heir Is Transforming Rural Arkansas Into a Design Powerhouse
item.description: Alice Walton is helping the Ozark region shed its “flyover” status by creating civic projects with top architects. The Waltons say they are “giving back.” What is the region giving up?
item.dc:creator: Sam Lubell
item.category: Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art
item.media:credit: Michael Davello for The New York Times
item.media:description: The 114,000-square-foot addition to the Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art in Bentonville, Ark., designed by Moshe Safdie, includes a glass-bridge gallery, right; a cafe, center and a contemporary art gallery, far left.

item.title: Can We Make a Dent in the Housing Crisis? Two Projects Say Yes.
item.description: As the Mamdani administration, and cities across America, grapple with affordable housing, two handsome complexes in Queens and Brooklyn show signs of progress.
item.dc:creator: Michael Kimmelman

item.title: If You Think You Know Brancusi’s Sculptures, Step Into His Studio
item.description: Rare artworks, photographs, films and tools have traveled from Paris to MoMA, revealing the father of modern sculpture as newly earthy.
item.dc:creator: Deborah Solomon
item.media:credit: Succession Brancusi, All rights reserved (Adagp/ARS); Photograph by Clement Pascal for The New York Times
item.media:description: The closing of the Pompidou Center for renovation has given MoMA a rare opportunity to bring Brancusi’s atelier to New York. It includes a film from his studio, above, and sculptures that combine wood and stone.

item.title: 25 Years After the World Trade Center Fell, an Architect’s Legacy Is Still Being Written
item.description: Our reporter’s personal journey in search of buildings by Minoru Yamasaki finds some abandoned, some celebrated.
item.dc:creator: Eric Lipton
item.media:credit: Library of Congress; Photo by Balthazar Korab Studios, Ltd.
item.media:description: The architect Minoru Yamasaki with model of the future World Trade Center, in the early 1970s.

item.title: Siena and the Art of the Butt
item.description: A show of bronzes at the Frick Collection reveals a divine and ancient craft they’d revived — and lessons in gluteal grace.
item.dc:creator: Blake Gopnik

item.title: Art Basel Paris to End Early Because of France Riots
item.description: Organizers cut the fair short after days of brisk sales at V.I.P. previews, citing safety concerns amid weeks of demonstrations in France.
item.dc:creator: Scott Reyburn
item.media:description: Visitors at Art Basel Paris on Wednesday.

item.title: Bumped From the National Mall, Smithsonian Folklife Fest Hit the Road
item.description: After being denied its customary spot on the National Mall, the Folklife Festival embarked on a nine-month journey through America’s local traditions.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Schuessler

item.title: Monet Painting Sells for $56 Million in France
item.description: The artwork, titled “Iris,” is among the painter’s later works, which wealthy collectors have coveted in recent years.
item.dc:creator: Scott Reyburn
item.media:description: Claude Monet’s “Iris" on display at Sotheby’s Paris before the auction.

item.title: Art Basel Las Vegas? The Fight Over Miami Beach’s Fair
item.description: After 18 months of negotiations and warnings that it might relocate to Nevada, the Art Basel fair will remain in Miami Beach through 2031.
item.dc:creator: Brett Sokol
item.media:description: Throngs of visitors to the opening of Art Basel Miami Beach last December at the Miami Beach Convention Center. After a vote last week, the fair’s new contract offers five more years and veto power over competing art events.

item.title: London Exhibition Displays Children’s Selfies as Art
item.description: An exhibition argues that juvenile photographic experiments can reveal unique perspectives worth saving — and even displaying.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Dickson
item.media:description: “Self-Portrait With Agifold,” by Robert Cooper, featured in “Snap Happy!”, an exhibit of photos taken by children at the Photographers’ Gallery in London.

item.title: Blurring the Line Between 3 Dimensions and 2
item.description: Torkwase Dyson’s latest paintings have a celestial depth that’s often reserved for sculpture.
item.dc:creator: Will Heinrich

item.title: Valor Mortis Upends the Soulslike Genre in First Person
item.description: With its first-person camera, Valor Mortis gives fans of the masochistic Soulslike genre a more intimate view of the action.
item.dc:creator: Justin Porter

item.title: She Signed Her Painting in 1548. Nearly 500 Years Later, It Finally Goes on Show.
item.description: Long overshadowed by her father and overlooked by historians, the 16th-century pioneer Catharina van Hemessen is now getting her due.
item.dc:creator: Valeriya Safronova

item.title: Art Gallery Shows to See in October
item.description: This week in Newly Reviewed, Will Heinrich covers Friedel Dzubas’s energetic squiggles, a group show with a milk crown, and an exhibition heavy on unfiltered self-expression.
item.dc:creator: Will Heinrich, Dawn Chan, Jillian Steinhauer and Travis Diehl

item.title: Rare Wartime Dissent in Moscow Over Plans to Dismantle Russia’s ‘Eiffel Tower’
item.description: A state broadcaster says it cannot afford the restoration of a 1922 steel tower, prompting rare wartime dissent and a movement to save the Modernist masterpiece.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Nechepurenko and Michael Kimmelman
item.category: Russian Television and Radio Broadcasting Network
item.media:description: The Shukhov Radio Tower was commissioned by Vladimir Lenin to spread the word of Communism across the vast Soviet territory.

item.title: The Photographers Who Helped Turn Marilyn Monroe Into a Global Star
item.description: The New York Historical exhibition explores the images that propelled the rise of Marilyn Monroe.
item.dc:creator: John Hanc
item.media:credit: Colin Clark for The New York Times
item.media:description: Photographs of Marilyn Monroe taken by Lawrence Schiller, including two Life covers, are on display in an exhibition at the New York Historical.

item.title: The Foundational Feminist Marianne Wex Takes Her Place at MoMA
item.description: An exhibition is built around the German artist Marianne Wex, whose photos are in dialogue with the works of others.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca L. Davis
item.media:credit: Colin Clark for The New York Times
item.media:description: Visitors looking at photographs from K8 Hardy’s “Position Series.” Hardy is one of seven contemporary artists featured alongside selections from a monumental project by the West German artist Marianne Wex, on view through May 2 at MoMA.

item.title: Rural Get-Togethers Celebrate Art and America’s 250th Anniversary
item.description: The idea is to bring people together in places that are not always thought of as art hubs, and produce new art along the way.
item.dc:creator: Ted Loos
item.media:credit: Kaoly Gutierrez for The New York Times
item.media:description: The artist Mel Chin at his property in the Blue Ridge Mountains in North Carolina, where he hosted a “Why We Gather” event.

item.title: Alex Da Corte Takes On Roy Lichtenstein and Marisol
item.description: The artist Alex Da Corte offers a fresh take on Roy Lichtenstein and Marisol in two new projects opening back-to-back this fall.
item.dc:creator: Hilarie M. Sheets
item.media:credit: Hannah Yoon for The New York Times
item.media:description: The artist Alex Da Corte, at his cavernous studio in Philadelphia, arranges figures for his feature-length video depiction of Marisol’s “The Party,” debuting Dec. 11 at the Buffalo AKG Art Museum.

item.title: In Vienna, a Celebration of Handmade Ceramics and Iconic Austrian Design
item.description: The women behind the housewares brand Carolina Irving & Daughters invited friends to a dinner to mark the launch of their new Wiener Werkstätte-inspired collection.
item.dc:creator: Tas Tóbiás

item.title: Ursula von Rydingsvard, Sculptor of Monumental Forms, Dies at 84
item.description: Working with four-by-four cedar beams, she created towering sculptures that evoked cave walls, frozen waves, seashells or the folds of a giant’s brain.
item.dc:creator: Will Heinrich
item.media:description: Ms. von Rydingsvard working on her sculpture “Ona” in 2013.

item.title: A Showcase of Works by the Designer Gio Ponti in New York
item.description: From skyscrapers to chairs to whimsical coat hooks, the Milan native Gio Ponti, who died in 1979, left an extraordinary legacy.
item.dc:creator: Shivani Vora
item.media:credit: Daniel Terna for The New York Times
item.media:description: Paul Donzella, the founder and owner of Donzella Project Space and Donzella Ltd. in New York City, worked with Brian Kish to curate “Gio Ponti: Designing Optimism,” a selling exhibition of Ponti’s work.

item.title: A New Exhibition Focuses on Ragtime at the Morgan Library & Museum
item.description: It is one of music’s most enduring genres, but its role in American culture has often been lost to time. This exhibition is aiming to change that.
item.dc:creator: Fahima Haque

item.title: The Denver Art Museum Explores the Diva Universe
item.description: Against a glittering backdrop and to the beat of a powerful soundtrack, an art museum exhibition gives the Dollys, Whitneys and Marías their due.
item.dc:creator: Megan McCrea and Amanda Villarosa

item.title: Across the U.S., Neon Signs Are Being Celebrated at Museums and Parks
item.description: Across the United States, from Nevada to Missouri, museums and parks are displaying and honoring signs that “are like jewels on a necklace of the road.”
item.dc:creator: Ken Belson

item.title: The Science Behind Your Reaction to Art
item.description: The Honolulu Museum of Art is showing how art can influence thinking, perspective and mood, in an exhibition that is part of a trend by museums to mix science and art.
item.dc:creator: Michael Janofsky

item.title: A World War II Museum Brings the Lessons of War to a Younger Audience
item.description: An idea sparked by the historian Stephen E. Ambrose became the National World War II Museum in New Orleans.
item.dc:creator: Claudia Dreifus
item.category: National World War II Museum (New Orleans, La)

item.title: Elaine de Kooning Gets Her Time in the Spotlight
item.description: A show at the Berry Campbell gallery in Manhattan offers a rare extensive examination of work by the artist, whose reputation has always been complicated by that of her famous husband.
item.dc:creator: Ted Loos

item.title: Jane Benson Makes Frankenstein’s Monster Sing
item.description: In the show “her her,” Jane Benson anatomizes Mary Shelley’s novel, highlighting its feminism and creating visual works that are also vocal scores.
item.dc:creator: Laurel Graeber
item.media:credit: Oliver Farshi for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jane Benson has created a new show called “her her” in which she imagines the monster in Mary Shelley’s “Frankenstein” speaking in the voice of an enraged woman.

item.title: Amsterdam’s Drift Museum Is a New Place to Experiment With Light and Form
item.description: A new art destination in Amsterdam will be filled with experiments in light and form.
item.dc:creator: Gisela Williams

item.title: Su Wu Celebrates Her Book “Mesoamerican Modern” at Mexico City’s Casa Möbius
item.description: To toast her new design book, “Mesoamerican Modern,” Su Wu co-hosted a dinner at Mexico City’s Casa Möbius.
item.dc:creator: Suleman Anaya
item.category: Mesoamerican Modern: Ancient Ideas in Contemporary Mexican Homes (Book)
